FEATURE: environments PREVIEW and PRODUCTION per goal. The daemon generates the infrastructure files from the approved contract's deployment requirements when the repository lacks them (multi-stage Dockerfile for the profile, docker-compose with app + postgres, healthcheck), landed through the lander. The human names a deploy TARGET per environment on the goal (local docker, or an SSH host `user@host` with docker installed; same card pattern as the publish remote) via `deployment.set_target`. `deployment.deploy {goalRef, environment}` (human-only): build the image at the landed HEAD sha (tag = sha), ship it (local: docker run; ssh: `docker save | ssh docker load`), replace the running container atomically, probe the health URL until 200 (timeout -> refuse), record `moe-deploy-receipt/1` {environment, sha, imageDigest, url, DEPLOYED|REFUSED(code)}; the previous receipt is kept for rollback (this row stores it; the row 'Monitoring, backup and rollback' consumes it). THE CASE NO CHILD OWNS, CONFIRMED PRESENT: a candidate that answers healthy ONCE and crashes seconds later leaves the environment down with nothing to restore it. `awaitHealthy` (:219-224) returns on the FIRST poll reading `healthy`; docker flips to `healthy` on the first passing check (the generated HEALTHCHECK's `--retries=20` governs the flip to UNHEALTHY, not to healthy). By then the receipt is committed and the incumbent is stopped. Recovery is an operator-initiated rollback — `rollback-command.ts` exists and is pinned by `imageDigest` — so the product has an answer, but it is MANUAL and nothing watches. Natural owner: task-7683a432 (monitoring/backup/rollback). Recorded here per global rail 21; not silently swallowed and not fixed in a roll-up row that owns zero production paths.

(b) ACCIDENTAL PRODUCTION — GENUINELY DEFENDED AGAINST THE CROSS-ROW MISTAKE, WEAKER AGAINST THE DOUBLE-CLICK. `goal-deployments.tsx:138` holds `armed` as a STRING KEYED BY ENVIRONMENT, not a boolean, and :211-212 make a click on an unarmed row RE-ARM it instead of dispatching — so arming preview and then clicking production can never fire production, which is the failure a boolean would have shipped (the publish card's boolean is safe only because it has one target). The confirm label is `Confirm: deploy to ${environment}` (:217), the aria-label is `Deploy this goal to ${environment}`, and PRODUCTION additionally renders its release standing at :196-199. A `Do not deploy` escape sits beside it, and armed state is per-mount so a reload disarms.
WHAT IT DOES NOT DEFEND: arm and confirm are the SAME element in the SAME position, so a fast double-click on the RIGHT row arms and dispatches with the operator having read nothing. The button disables while in flight (:206) which stops a THIRD click, not the second. For preview that is cheap; for production it is one impatient double-click. Not a defect of this row's delivery — the environment-keying was the specified protection and it works — but it is the residual, and it belongs to whoever next touches that card.

HOW I GOT IT WRONG. I ran `docker version 2>&1 | head -12; echo "EXIT=$?"`. `$?` after a pipeline is the exit code of the LAST command — `head` — which always succeeds. I read head's 0 and attributed it to docker. This is the pipe hazard global rail 8 names in its own last sentence ("a piped run reports tail's exit code — capture ${PIPESTATUS[0]}").

THE MEASUREMENT, redone unpiped:
```
$ docker version > /tmp/dv.log 2>&1; echo "TRUE_EXIT=$?"
TRUE_EXIT=1
  (last line) failed to connect to the docker API at npipe:////./pipe/dockerDesktopLinuxEngine;
  check if the path is correct and if the daemon is running: open //./pipe/dockerDesktopLinuxEngine:
  The system cannot find the file specified.

$ docker --version > /tmp/dv2.log 2>&1; echo "EXIT=$?"
EXIT=0
Docker version 29.6.2, build dfc4efb
```
So the two probes differ exactly as the runbook says they do: `docker version` (talks to the engine) exits 1; `docker --version` (CLI only) exits 0 and proves nothing. The runbook's "**Check with `docker version`, never `docker --version`**" is correct guidance and I can now confirm it first-hand.

WHAT THIS CORRECTS BEYOND MY OWN NOTE. Child 1's APPROVED reviewSummary (task-3706b7e7) carries "Confirmed docker version fails yet EXITS 0, validating classify-on-server-version."   "Classifying on 'the binary was found' would call that host docker-capable and the build would
   then fail somewhere far less legible. Classifying on the exit status is no better: the status
   varies by docker build and is trivially swallowed by a pipe. So the discriminator is the one
   thing only a live daemon can produce — a parseable SERVER version on stdout."

So the reason is portability plus pipe-fragility, NOT "docker version exits 0". `classifyDockerProbe` (:49-65) is a pure function over `{spawnError, status, stdout, stderr}` that tests `stdout`'s first meaningful line against `/^\d+\.\d+(?:\.\d+)?/`; `status` is used only to enrich the refusal detail, never to decide.
